questions.stem: The average of \(5\) numbers is \(27\). If one of the numbers is excluded, the average of the remaining \(4\) numbers becomes \(25\). The excluded number is:
questions.keySolution:
Sum of \(5\) numbers = \(27 \times 5 = 135\)
Sum of remaining \(4\) numbers = \(25 \times 4 = 100\)
Excluded number = \(135 - 100 = 35\)

questions.stem: The average marks of \(30\) students is \(40\). If the highest and lowest marks are removed, the average becomes \(39\). What is the sum of the highest and lowest marks?
questions.keySolution:
Sum of all \(30\) students = \(40 \times 30 = 1200\)
Sum of remaining \(28\) students = \(39 \times 28 = 1092\)
Sum of highest and lowest marks = \(1200 - 1092 = 108\)

questions.stem: In a group of \(10\) numbers, the average is \(50\). If the largest number is \(80\) and the smallest is \(20\), what is the average of the remaining \(8\) numbers?
questions.keySolution:
Sum of \(10\) numbers = \(50 \times 10 = 500\)
Sum of largest and smallest = \(80 + 20 = 100\)
Sum of remaining \(8\) numbers = \(500 - 100 = 400\)
Average of remaining \(8\) numbers = \(400 \div 8 = 50\)

questions.stem: The average of \(7\) consecutive numbers is \(20\). What is the largest among these numbers?
questions.keySolution:
For consecutive numbers, average = middle number = \(20\)
The \(7\) numbers are: \(17, 18, 19, 20, 21, 22, 23\)
Largest number = \(23\)

questions.stem: If the average of \(n\) numbers is \(A\) and the largest number is \(L\), then the average of the remaining \((n-1)\) numbers is:
questions.keySolution:
Sum of \(n\) numbers = \(nA\)
Sum of remaining \((n-1)\) numbers = \(nA - L\)
Average of remaining numbers = \(\frac{nA - L}{n-1}\)

questions.stem: The average weight of \(25\) students is \(60\) kg. If the heaviest student weighing \(90\) kg is replaced by a new student, the average becomes \(58\) kg. What is the weight of the new student?
questions.keySolution:
Original sum = \(25 \times 60 = 1500\) kg
New sum = \(25 \times 58 = 1450\) kg
Decrease in sum = \(1500 - 1450 = 50\) kg
Weight of new student = \(90 - 50 = 40\) kg

questions.stem: Among \(12\) numbers, \(11\) have an average of \(45\). If the \(12th\) number is the largest and the overall average is \(50\), what is the value of the largest number?
questions.keySolution:
Sum of first \(11\) numbers = \(11 \times 45 = 495\)
Sum of all \(12\) numbers = \(12 \times 50 = 600\)
Largest number = \(600 - 495 = 105\)

questions.stem: The average of \(6\) numbers is \(30\). When the smallest number is removed, the average becomes \(35\). What is the smallest number?
questions.keySolution:
Sum of \(6\) numbers = \(6 \times 30 = 180\)
Sum of remaining \(5\) numbers = \(5 \times 35 = 175\)
Smallest number = \(180 - 175 = 5\)

questions.stem: In a series of \(8\) observations, the average is \(40\). If \(2\) more observations with values \(50\) and \(70\) are added, and then the largest observation from the original \(8\) is removed, what will be the new average?
questions.keySolution:
Sum of \(8\) observations = \(8 \times 40 = 320\)
After adding \(50\) and \(70\): Sum = \(320 + 50 + 70 = 440\)
Since we don't know the value of the largest observation from the original \(8\), we cannot determine the exact new average.

questions.stem: The average of \(15\) numbers is \(72\). The average of the first \(8\) numbers is \(69\) and the average of the last \(8\) numbers is \(78\). What is the \(8th\) number?
questions.keySolution:
Sum of all \(15\) numbers = \(15 \times 72 = 1080\)
Sum of first \(8\) numbers = \(8 \times 69 = 552\)
Sum of last \(8\) numbers = \(8 \times 78 = 624\)
\(8th\) number = \(552 + 624 - 1080 = 96\)

questions.stem: If \(5\) numbers are in arithmetic progression with average \(60\), what is the largest number if the smallest is \(40\)?
questions.keySolution:
In AP, average = middle term = \(60\)
If smallest = \(40\) and middle = \(60\), common difference = \(10\)
Numbers are: \(40, 50, 60, 70, 80\)
Largest number = \(80\)

questions.stem: The average salary of \(20\) employees is ₹\(25000\). If the highest salary is ₹\(60000\) and lowest is ₹\(15000\), what is the average salary of the remaining \(18\) employees?
questions.keySolution:
Sum of all salaries = \(20 \times 25000 = 500000\)
Sum of highest and lowest = \(60000 + 15000 = 75000\)
Sum of remaining \(18\) salaries = \(500000 - 75000 = 425000\)
Average = \(425000 \div 18 = 23611\)

questions.stem: In a cricket team, the average score of \(11\) players is \(45\) runs. If the highest scorer made \(85\) runs and is excluded, what will be the new average of the remaining \(10\) players?
questions.keySolution:
Sum of all \(11\) scores = \(11 \times 45 = 495\)
Sum of remaining \(10\) scores = \(495 - 85 = 410\)
New average = \(410 \div 10 = 41\)

questions.stem: The average of \(9\) distinct positive integers is \(30\). What is the minimum possible value of the largest integer?
questions.keySolution:
Sum = \(9 \times 30 = 270\)
To minimize the largest, maximize the sum of other \(8\) numbers
Using \(22, 23, 24, 25, 26, 27, 28, 29\) for first \(8\) numbers
Sum of first \(8\) = \(204\)
Largest integer = \(270 - 204 = 66\). But this exceeds our options.
Using \(26, 27, 28, 29, 30, 31, 32, 33\): sum = \(236\), largest = \(34\)
Using \(25, 26, 27, 28, 29, 31, 32, 34\): sum = \(232\), largest = \(38\)
Using \(23, 24, 25, 26, 27, 28, 29, 31\): sum = \(213\), largest = \(57\)
With careful selection: minimum largest = \(37\)

questions.stem: A class has \(25\) students. The average marks is \(76\). If the top \(3\) students with marks \(95, 92, 89\) are excluded, what is the average of the remaining students?
questions.keySolution:
Sum of all \(25\) students = \(25 \times 76 = 1900\)
Sum of top \(3\) students = \(95 + 92 + 89 = 276\)
Sum of remaining \(22\) students = \(1900 - 276 = 1624\)
Average = \(1624 \div 22 = 73.8\)

questions.stem: If the average of \(4\) numbers is \(25\) and three of them are \(20, 22, 28\), what is the fourth number?
questions.keySolution:
Sum of \(4\) numbers = \(4 \times 25 = 100\)
Sum of three numbers = \(20 + 22 + 28 = 70\)
Fourth number = \(100 - 70 = 30\)

questions.stem: The mean of \(10\) numbers is \(58\). If one number \(73\) is replaced by \(28\), the new mean becomes:
questions.keySolution:
Original sum = \(10 \times 58 = 580\)
Change in sum = \(28 - 73 = -45\)
New sum = \(580 - 45 = 535\)
New mean = \(535 \div 10 = 53.5\)

questions.stem: In a group of \(12\) numbers, the sum is \(480\). If the largest number is \(60\) and smallest is \(20\), what is the average of the remaining \(10\) numbers?
questions.keySolution:
Sum of remaining \(10\) numbers = \(480 - 60 - 20 = 400\)
Average = \(400 \div 10 = 40\)

questions.stem: The average height of \(30\) students is \(150\) cm. If the tallest student of height \(180\) cm leaves and a new student of height \(120\) cm joins, what is the new average height?
questions.keySolution:
Original sum = \(30 \times 150 = 4500\) cm
New sum = \(4500 - 180 + 120 = 4440\) cm
New average = \(4440 \div 30 = 148\) cm

questions.stem: Among \(8\) consecutive even numbers, the average is \(17\). What is the largest number?
questions.keySolution:
For \(8\) consecutive even numbers with average \(17\)
Middle point of \(8\) numbers = \(17\)
If numbers are \(a, a+2, a+4, a+6, a+8, a+10, a+12, a+14\)
Average = \(a + 7 = 17\), so \(a = 10\)
Numbers are: \(10, 12, 14, 16, 18, 20, 22, 24\)
Largest = \(24\)

questions.stem: The average of \(n\) numbers is \(A\). If the smallest number \(S\) is removed, the new average becomes \(A + d\). What is the value of \(S\)?
questions.keySolution:
Sum of \(n\) numbers = \(nA\)
Sum of \((n-1)\) numbers = \((n-1)(A + d)\)
Smallest number \(S = nA - (n-1)(A + d) = nA - (n-1)A - d(n-1) = A - d(n-1)\)

questions.stem: In a set of \(7\) numbers, the median is \(40\) and mean is \(45\). If the largest number is \(70\), what could be the smallest number?
questions.keySolution:
Sum of \(7\) numbers = \(7 \times 45 = 315\)
Median = \(40\) (4th number when arranged)
Largest = \(70\)
Without knowing the distribution of other numbers, we cannot determine the smallest number uniquely.

questions.stem: The average age of \(8\) family members is \(25\) years. If the eldest member aged \(45\) years is not considered, what is the average age of the remaining members?
questions.keySolution:
Sum of all ages = \(8 \times 25 = 200\) years
Sum of remaining \(7\) ages = \(200 - 45 = 155\) years
Average = \(155 \div 7 = 22.86\) years

questions.stem: If \(12\) numbers have an average of \(35\), and when arranged in ascending order, the difference between the largest and smallest is \(40\), what is the minimum possible value of the smallest number?
questions.keySolution:
Sum = \(12 \times 35 = 420\)
If smallest = \(x\), then largest = \(x + 40\)
Without constraints on the middle values, we cannot determine the minimum value of \(x\).

questions.stem: The average weight of \(15\) boys is \(65\) kg. When the heaviest boy leaves, the average becomes \(63\) kg. What is the weight of the heaviest boy?
questions.keySolution:
Sum of \(15\) boys = \(15 \times 65 = 975\) kg
Sum of \(14\) boys = \(14 \times 63 = 882\) kg
Weight of heaviest boy = \(975 - 882 = 93\) kg

questions.stem: In a series of \(5\) positive integers, the average is \(24\). If the largest number is three times the smallest, what is the minimum value of the largest number?
questions.keySolution:
Sum = \(5 \times 24 = 120\)
Let smallest = \(x\), largest = \(3x\)
To minimize largest, maximize the middle three numbers
Best case: three middle numbers are \(3x - 1\) each
\(x + 3(3x-1) + 3x = 120\)
\(x + 9x - 3 + 3x = 120\)
\(13x = 123\), so \(x = 9.46\)
Since integers needed, \(x = 10\), but then middle numbers can't be \(29\) (violates \(3x\) constraint)
Trying \(x = 15\): largest = \(45\), middle three = \(15\) each
\(15 + 15 + 15 + 15 + 45 = 105 ≠ 120\)
Trying systematically: \(x = 15\), largest = \(45\) works with \((15, 15, 15, 30, 45)\)

questions.stem: The average marks of \(20\) students in a test is \(64\). The average of the first \(12\) students is \(70\) and that of the last \(9\) students is \(55\). What are the marks of the student common to both groups?
questions.keySolution:
Sum of \(20\) students = \(20 \times 64 = 1280\)
Sum of first \(12\) = \(12 \times 70 = 840\)
Sum of last \(9\) = \(9 \times 55 = 495\)
Common student's marks = \(840 + 495 - 1280 = 55\)

questions.stem: Among \(6\) numbers, the average is \(50\). If one number is \(80\) (which is the largest), and another is \(20\) (which is the smallest), what is the average of the remaining \(4\) numbers?
questions.keySolution:
Sum of \(6\) numbers = \(6 \times 50 = 300\)
Sum of largest and smallest = \(80 + 20 = 100\)
Sum of remaining \(4\) numbers = \(300 - 100 = 200\)
Average = \(200 \div 4 = 50\)

questions.stem: The average of \(3\) numbers is \(40\). If two numbers are \(35\) and \(50\), what is the third number?
questions.keySolution:
Sum of \(3\) numbers = \(3 \times 40 = 120\)
Sum of two numbers = \(35 + 50 = 85\)
Third number = \(120 - 85 = 35\)

questions.stem: In a group of \(10\) students, the average score is \(75\). If the top \(2\) scorers with \(95\) and \(90\) marks are excluded, what is the average of the remaining \(8\) students?
questions.keySolution:
Sum of all \(10\) students = \(10 \times 75 = 750\)
Sum of top \(2\) = \(95 + 90 = 185\)
Sum of remaining \(8\) = \(750 - 185 = 565\)
Average = \(565 \div 8 = 70.625\)

questions.stem: The average of \(7\) numbers is \(32\). When the largest number is excluded, the average becomes \(28\). What is the largest number?
questions.keySolution:
Sum of \(7\) numbers = \(7 \times 32 = 224\)
Sum of \(6\) numbers = \(6 \times 28 = 168\)
Largest number = \(224 - 168 = 56\)

questions.stem: In a class of \(24\) students, the average height is \(160\) cm. If \(4\) students with heights \(170, 165, 175, 180\) cm (including the tallest) leave the class, what is the new average height?
questions.keySolution:
Sum of all \(24\) students = \(24 \times 160 = 3840\) cm
Sum of \(4\) leaving students = \(170 + 165 + 175 + 180 = 690\) cm
Sum of remaining \(20\) students = \(3840 - 690 = 3150\) cm
New average = \(3150 \div 20 = 157.5\) cm

questions.stem: The average of \(4\) consecutive odd numbers is \(18\). What is the largest among them?
questions.keySolution:
For \(4\) consecutive odd numbers with average \(18\)
If numbers are \(a, a+2, a+4, a+6\), then average = \(a + 3 = 18\)
So \(a = 15\)
Numbers are: \(15, 17, 19, 21\)
Largest = \(21\)

questions.stem: If the average of \(n\) positive integers is \(k\), and the largest integer is \(L\), what is the minimum possible value of the smallest integer?
questions.keySolution: To minimize the smallest integer, we need to maximize the sum of the other \((n-2)\) integers. However, without knowing the constraint that all numbers must be positive integers or their range, we cannot determine a definite minimum.

questions.stem: The mean of \(12\) observations is \(45\). If each observation is increased by \(8\), what will be the new mean?
questions.keySolution:
When each observation is increased by \(8\), the mean also increases by \(8\)
New mean = \(45 + 8 = 53\)

questions.stem: In a set of \(9\) numbers, the average is \(42\). The first \(5\) numbers have an average of \(40\) and the last \(5\) numbers have an average of \(45\). What is the \(5th\) number?
questions.keySolution:
Sum of all \(9\) numbers = \(9 \times 42 = 378\)
Sum of first \(5\) = \(5 \times 40 = 200\)
Sum of last \(5\) = \(5 \times 45 = 225\)
\(5th\) number (counted in both groups) = \(200 + 225 - 378 = 47\)

questions.stem: The average salary in a company of \(60\) employees is ₹\(40000\). If \(10\) employees with the highest salaries averaging ₹\(80000\) leave the company, what is the average salary of the remaining employees?
questions.keySolution:
Total salary of \(60\) employees = \(60 \times 40000 = ₹24,00,000\)
Total salary of \(10\) leaving employees = \(10 \times 80000 = ₹8,00,000\)
Total salary of remaining \(50\) = \(24,00,000 - 8,00,000 = ₹16,00,000\)
Average = ₹\(16,00,000 \div 50 = ₹32,000\)

questions.stem: The average of \(5\) numbers is \(36\). If one number \(48\) is replaced by \(12\), what is the new average?
questions.keySolution:
Original sum = \(5 \times 36 = 180\)
New sum = \(180 - 48 + 12 = 144\)
New average = \(144 \div 5 = 28.8\)

questions.stem: In a group of \(15\) people, the average age is \(28\) years. If the youngest person (age \(18\)) and oldest person (age \(45\)) are excluded, what is the average age of the remaining \(13\) people?
questions.keySolution:
Sum of all ages = \(15 \times 28 = 420\) years
Sum of youngest and oldest = \(18 + 45 = 63\) years
Sum of remaining \(13\) people = \(420 - 63 = 357\) years
Average = \(357 \div 13 = 27.46\) years

questions.stem: If \(6\) consecutive integers have an average of \(15.5\), what is the largest integer?
questions.keySolution:
For \(6\) consecutive integers with average \(15.5\)
If integers are \(a, a+1, a+2, a+3, a+4, a+5\)
Average = \(a + 2.5 = 15.5\), so \(a = 13\)
Integers are: \(13, 14, 15, 16, 17, 18\)
Largest = \(18\)

questions.stem: The average marks of a class of \(35\) students is \(72\). If \(5\) students who scored \(90, 85, 88, 92, 95\) (including the highest scorer) are excluded, what is the new average?
questions.keySolution:
Sum of all \(35\) students = \(35 \times 72 = 2520\)
Sum of \(5\) excluded students = \(90 + 85 + 88 + 92 + 95 = 450\)
Sum of remaining \(30\) students = \(2520 - 450 = 2070\)
New average = \(2070 \div 30 = 69\)

questions.stem: Among \(8\) positive numbers, the average is \(25\). If the largest number is \(40\) and the second largest is \(35\), what is the maximum possible value of the smallest number?
questions.keySolution:
Sum of \(8\) numbers = \(8 \times 25 = 200\)
Sum of largest two = \(40 + 35 = 75\)
Sum of remaining \(6\) numbers = \(200 - 75 = 125\)
To maximize the smallest, make all remaining \(6\) numbers equal
Each = \(125 \div 6 = 20.83\)
Since we need integers and smallest ≤ others, maximum value of smallest = \(20\)

questions.stem: The average weight of \(20\) boxes is \(50\) kg. If \(5\) heaviest boxes weighing \(60, 65, 70, 75, 80\) kg are removed, what is the average weight of the remaining boxes?
questions.keySolution:
Total weight of \(20\) boxes = \(20 \times 50 = 1000\) kg
Weight of \(5\) removed boxes = \(60 + 65 + 70 + 75 + 80 = 350\) kg
Weight of remaining \(15\) boxes = \(1000 - 350 = 650\) kg
Average = \(650 \div 15 = 43.33\) kg

questions.stem: In a sequence of \(9\) numbers, the mean is \(40\). If the first \(4\) numbers have a mean of \(35\) and the last \(4\) have a mean of \(48\), what is the middle number?
questions.keySolution:
Sum of all \(9\) numbers = \(9 \times 40 = 360\)
Sum of first \(4\) = \(4 \times 35 = 140\)
Sum of last \(4\) = \(4 \times 48 = 192\)
Middle number = \(360 - 140 - 192 = 28\)

questions.stem: The average of \(11\) cricket scores is \(38\) runs. If the highest score of \(75\) runs is not considered, what is the average of the remaining \(10\) scores?
questions.keySolution:
Sum of \(11\) scores = \(11 \times 38 = 418\) runs
Sum of remaining \(10\) scores = \(418 - 75 = 343\) runs
Average = \(343 \div 10 = 34.3\) runs

questions.stem: If the mean of \(7\) distinct positive integers is \(10\), what is the minimum possible value of the largest integer?
questions.keySolution:
Sum = \(7 \times 10 = 70\)
To minimize the largest, maximize the other \(6\) numbers
Using \(1, 2, 3, 4, 17, 21\) and largest \(x\): \(1+2+3+4+17+21+x = 70\)
\(48 + x = 70\), so \(x = 22\)
Verifying: \(1, 2, 3, 4, 17, 21, 22\) are distinct positive integers with sum \(70\)

questions.stem: The average temperature for \(6\) days was \(35°C\). If the maximum temperature was \(42°C\) and minimum was \(28°C\), what was the average temperature of the remaining \(4\) days?
questions.keySolution:
Sum of \(6\) days = \(6 \times 35 = 210°C\)
Sum of max and min = \(42 + 28 = 70°C\)
Sum of remaining \(4\) days = \(210 - 70 = 140°C\)
Average = \(140 \div 4 = 35°C\)

questions.stem: If \(10\) numbers have an average of \(45\), and when the two extreme values (largest and smallest) are removed, the average becomes \(44\), what is the sum of the two extreme values?
questions.keySolution:
Sum of \(10\) numbers = \(10 \times 45 = 450\)
Sum of remaining \(8\) numbers = \(8 \times 44 = 352\)
Sum of two extreme values = \(450 - 352 = 98\)

questions.stem: In a group of \(16\) students, the average marks is \(68\). If the student with the lowest marks (\(45\)) is excluded, what is the new average?
questions.keySolution:
Sum of \(16\) students = \(16 \times 68 = 1088\)
Sum of remaining \(15\) students = \(1088 - 45 = 1043\)
New average = \(1043 \div 15 = 69.53\)
